4.0.0.en: 1 Thou also, son of man, take thee a tile, and lay it before thee, and pourtray upon it the city, even Jerusalem: 2 And lay siege against it, and build a fort against it, and cast a mount against it; set the camp also against it, and set battering rams against it round about. 3 Moreover take thou unto thee an iron pan, and set it for a wall of iron between thee and the city: and set thy face against it, and it shall be besieged, and thou shalt lay siege against it. This shall be a sign to the house of Israel.

4.0.1.en: The Lord commanded him to draw on a tile (a brick of clay) a city besieged by armies, and to set against it a fort, a mount and battering rams (war machines for demolishing walls), declaring that the siege of Jerusalem was coming by divine permission for chastisement, since the holy Temple had for many long years been defiled by the setting up of images of idols and pagan gods inside the holy places.

4.0.2.en: When Zion felt that the Lord had forsaken her and her Lord had forgotten her, He assured her: "Behold, I have graven thee upon the palms of my hands" (Isa 49:16). I have engraved you in My Son Jesus Christ, since you are His holy body and He is the Head; I see you in Him holy and justified, lifted up through Him and in Him into My embrace, enjoying fellowship in My glories. Here, however, since Zion insists on sin and clings to temporal things and does not want to rise above earthly things, God asked Ezekiel to draw her on a tile of clay, instead of being drawn on the palm of the Lord; He gives her the desire of her heart. Therefore He often repeats such a phrase: "I will recompense thy ways upon thee" (Ezek 7:4). She desired the earth, so He made her engraved on clay!! After the names of the tribes of Israel were engraved on precious stones placed on the breast of the high priest, that he might enter with them into the Holy of Holies in the shadow of the heavenlies, behold the city of Jerusalem is engraved on the clay with which she wanted to be weighed down!

4.1.0.en: In the Song of Songs God prides Himself on His children, comparing them to the horses working together in one spirit in His divine chariot for salvation (Song 1:9); He sees them as comely as Tirzah, terrible as an army with banners (Song 6:4)... But since they insist on withdrawing from Him and clinging to abominations, He raises against them from the nations a fort, a mount and battering rams to shatter every strength in them! He even commands the setting up of a wall of iron around the city [3], not to protect it but so that no one may escape the chastisements that come upon it!

4.2.0.en: The wonder is that God, in the midst of this bitterness, asks the prophet more than once to set his face against the city (Ezek 3:7) and to have his arm uncovered when he prophesies against it [7]. The affirmation, twice, of setting his face against the besieged city is a sign of God's care for His people, from the Jews as from the Gentiles; the Church, of all races, is the object of His care, His providence and His concern even in the bitterest moments of chastisement. He permits His children afflictions with all their bitterness, and with them salvation. Therefore St. John Chrysostom calls suffering "the school of philosophy," and says: [When we sin, God raises our enemies against us to chastise us; therefore it is fitting for us not to fight them, but to call ourselves to account and instruct ourselves. Let us receive sufferings as we receive medicines from the physician for our salvation, and as we receive chastisement from a father so that we may be glorified. Therefore the wise Ben Sira says: My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thyself for temptation and endure].

4.2.1.en: As for the uncovered arm, it points to the divine Incarnation, for the Fathers see in "the arm of the Lord" a reference to the Son, and in "the finger of the Lord" a reference to the Holy Spirit. It is as though Jerusalem remains under siege in the grip of sin and under its dominion until the arm of the Lord is uncovered, as St. John says: "For the life was manifested, and we have seen it, and bear witness, and shew unto you that eternal life, which was with the Father, and was manifested unto us" (1 Jn 1:5). He who is invisible became, by the Incarnation, uncovered, for He "dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth" (Jn 1:14). Our heart, the inner Jerusalem, was besieged and our temple defiled and we were in a state of death, until the Father bared His arm, that is, sent His only Son to free us and bring us back to salvation. This is what the prophet Isaiah saw by the spirit of prophecy when he proclaimed good tidings to Jerusalem, captive to sin, which had slept the sleep of death and been buried in the dust and utterly shattered, saying:

4.2.2.en: "Awake, awake; put on thy strength, O Zion;

4.2.3.en: put on thy beautiful garments, O Jerusalem, the holy city.

4.2.4.en: Shake thyself from the dust; arise, and sit down, O Jerusalem: loose thyself from the bands of thy neck, O captive daughter of Zion.

4.2.5.en: How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of him that bringeth good tidings, that publisheth peace; that bringeth good tidings of good, that publisheth salvation; that saith unto Zion, Thy God reigneth!...

4.2.6.en: Break forth into joy, sing together, ye waste places of Jerusalem: for the LORD hath comforted his people, he hath redeemed Jerusalem. The LORD hath made bare his holy arm in the eyes of all the nations; and all the ends of the earth shall see the salvation of our God" (Isa 52).

4.2.7.en: It is clear that the secret of Zion's awakening, her putting on her strength, her shaking herself from the dust, her freedom from the bands of slavery around her neck, and her enjoyment of peace, is the baring of the arm of the Lord in the eyes of the nations, that is, the Incarnation of the Lord to gather into His body congregations enjoying salvation.

4.2.8.en: Moreover, the baring of the arm points to readiness to strike, and as I believe He does not mean striking His people but striking the sin that shattered this people, for the Lord Christ came not to condemn man but to save him... He condemned the sin into which we had fallen, in His body!

4.2.9.en: God's heart toward His people has not changed, but His holiness requires the shattering of sin and the punishment of the wicked who persist in their evil, that perhaps they may return to Him in repentance.

4.3.0.en: 4 Lie thou also upon thy left side, and lay the iniquity of the house of Israel upon it: according to the number of the days that thou shalt lie upon it thou shalt bear their iniquity. 5 For I have laid upon thee the years of their iniquity, according to the number of the days, three hundred and ninety days: so shalt thou bear the iniquity of the house of Israel. 6 And when thou hast accomplished them, lie again on thy right side, and thou shalt bear the iniquity of the house of Judah forty days: I have appointed thee each day for a year. 7 Therefore thou shalt set thy face toward the siege of Jerusalem, and thine arm shall be uncovered, and thou shalt prophesy against it. 8 And, behold, I will lay bands upon thee, and thou shalt not turn thee from one side to another, till thou hast ended the days of thy siege.

4.3.1.en: Having declared the siege of Jerusalem and her captivity, with a hint of His concern for her and of the baring of the arm of His holiness for her salvation, the Lord began to make clear the effect of sin in the life of man: it shatters him completely, casts him into a state of continual sleep without vitality or work, man lying on one side like one stricken with palsy (paralysis).

4.3.2.en: He asked him to lie on his left side 390 days (and according to the Septuagint 190 days), then to return and lie on his right side for forty days; the first lying points to the iniquity of the house of Israel and the second to the house of Judah. The first work points to man's falling under the authority of the left-hand stroke, that is, the visible sins such as fornication, murder, theft, lying and so on, while the right-hand stroke is the hidden sins to which believers and those who serve the Lord are exposed, such as the sins of self-righteousness and love of honor and praise, things that have not the appearance of sin before people but corrupt the lives of believers and servants. Lying on the left side lasts a longer time than lying on the right side, because the people of Judah, although they were later in their evil than the northern kingdom of Israel, completed their evil in a short time. Thus by the right-hand strokes believers fall with dangerous speed, and their evil is completed in a short time, which made St. John Chrysostom declare: [I marvel at a bishop (a head) who is saved!], just as the desert Fathers used to warn their sons the monks against the right-hand strokes more than the left-hand ones, because the latter are clear and repentance for them is easy, while the former are often hidden, creeping into the heart and shattering its repentance!

4.3.3.en: Why was the left side ascribed to Israel and the right to Judah? Because when a man looks toward the rising of the sun the north is on his left and the south on his right; so Israel, the northern kingdom, is represented by his left side, and Judah, the southern kingdom, is represented by his right side.

4.3.4.en: As for the numbers, I do not wish to enter into many details, since various interpretations have been found for them, so I am content here to highlight the following points:

4.3.5.en: a. Some see that by adding the two numbers together (390+40) the result is 430 days, a symbol of the years of bondage which the Jewish nation lived in Egypt under slavery. It is as though these numbers are only a symbol of the effect of sin in the life of believers, as it brings them into bitter bondage.

4.3.6.en: b. Some see that the number 390 points to the years Israel lived from the apostasy of Jeroboam until the destruction of Jerusalem, while the number 40 points to the years in which Judah declined before the captivity.

4.3.7.en: c. Some interpret the number 390 thus: the siege of Jerusalem lasted 18 months (Jer 52:4-6); if five months are removed from it, in which the besiegers withdrew when the army of Pharaoh approached (Jer 37:5-8), the remainder is 13 months, that is, 390 days.

4.3.8.en: d. The two numbers 390 and 40 symbolize the sin that has included every man and included all temporal life, shattering all humanity with its palsy, and shattering each one all the days of his time. The number 390 is the product of multiplying 39 by 10, because the number of the tribes of the kingdom of Israel is (10), and the wages of evil are 39 stripes, as though all the tribes had deserved the scourging. As for the number 40, it points to the whole temporal life; therefore the Lord Christ fasted forty days, and so did Moses and Elijah, a sign of the necessity of our asceticism all the days of our exile. So the first number means that sin includes the life of all people, and the second that it includes all the days of our time.

4.3.9.en: Some see that what is stated here about his lying 390 days on his left side and 40 days on his right side contradicts what is stated in (Ezek 8:1), where we find the prophet sitting among the elders of his people during the mentioned period, besides the contradiction of this command of God to him with human ability, for it is inconceivable that Ezekiel was able to carry it out.

4.3.10.en: The reply to this: the preceding text includes an ancient Eastern custom, namely the custom of men "reclining" while sitting on the ground, resting on a cushion placed under the right or left hand, according to the person's wish.

4.4.0.en: The mentioned text does not require the prophet's immobility during the carrying out of the Lord's command, but requires of him the necessity of committing to recline on his left side during the 390 days and on the right side during the 40 days whenever he wished to sit only, and it also required the necessity of uncovering the whole arm on which he reclines [7]. This command does not contradict the prophet's practicing everything he wants of various movements and works during the mentioned period, and we find no difficulty for the prophet or for anyone else in practicing this command. Nor do we find any contradiction with the text in (Ezek 8:1) concerning the sitting of the prophet Ezekiel among the elders of his people. The first text does not forbid the prophet to sit with others, and at the same time affirms that he was sitting in his house, that is, reclining, and without doubt he was committed to the position that the divine revelation specified for him, so there is no disagreement between the two texts.

4.5.s.en: 3. Eating by weight and with care:

4.5.0.en: 9 Take thou also unto thee wheat, and barley, and beans, and lentiles, and millet, and fitches, and put them in one vessel, and make thee bread thereof, according to the number of the days that thou shalt lie upon thy side, three hundred and ninety days shalt thou eat thereof. 10 And thy meat which thou shalt eat shall be by weight, twenty shekels a day: from time to time shalt thou eat it. 11 Thou shalt drink also water by measure, the sixth part of an hin: from time to time shalt thou drink. 12 And thou shalt eat it as barley cakes, and thou shalt bake it with dung that cometh out of man, in their sight. 13 And the LORD said, Even thus shall the children of Israel eat their defiled bread among the Gentiles, whither I will drive them. 14 Then said I, Ah Lord GOD! behold, my soul hath not been polluted: for from my youth up even till now have I not eaten of that which dieth of itself, or is torn in pieces; neither came there abominable flesh into my mouth. 15 Then he said unto me, Lo, I have given thee cow's dung for man's dung, and thou shalt prepare thy bread therewith. 16 Moreover he said unto me, Son of man, behold, I will break the staff of bread in Jerusalem: and they shall eat bread by weight, and with care; and they shall drink water by measure, and with astonishment: 17 That they may want bread and water, and be astonied one with another, and consume away for their iniquity.

4.5.1.en: Eating by weight and with care, and drinking by measure and with astonishment, is a sign of the famine that comes upon the people for chastisement. It is a symbol of the work of sin in the life of man, as it afflicts his soul with a state of hunger with care and thirst with astonishment... all this besides the palsy (paralysis) that has struck it.

4.5.2.en: He fixed for him ten shekels (about 8 ounces) of bread each day, and a sixth of a hin (about half a pint or 16/1 of a gallon) of water. The bread was of the poorest kinds, such as is given to horses and swine, a mixture of wheat, barley, beans, lentils, millet (sorghum) and vetch (a wild seed like wheat), which he ate while lying on one side. He also asked him to bake it using human excrement instead of firewood, a sign of the defilement and uncleanness the people had reached (Deut 23:13-14), but when he pleaded with Him to excuse him from this, He allowed him to bake it on animal dung. This custom is still found in some villages of Upper Egypt, where dried dung (the galla) is used as fuel instead of firewood. In any case this action symbolizes the hardship to which the people come!

4.5.3.en: In Your love You engraved me on Your palms

4.5.4.en: * In Your love You engraved me on Your palm, O my God; You counted me beloved Jerusalem and holy Zion.

4.5.5.en: But by my sins and the uncleannesses of my heart I became engraved on a tile of clay.

4.5.6.en: I became despised, wallowing in the mire.

4.5.7.en: Through my negligence the enemy surrounded me and shattered my walls, O You who desire to set up Your fiery Spirit as a wall for my life!

4.5.8.en: * You stretched out, O Father, Your divine arm, when You sent me Your Son incarnate, to wash me from the dust, and give me Your fiery Spirit, and carry me to Your embrace!

4.5.9.en: * My sin has removed my vitality from me; I became sick with palsy, at one time reclining on my left side, struck by evils, and at another reclining on the right, struck by self-righteousness. * My sin deprived me of satisfaction, and turned my inner paradise into a desolate wasteland.

4.5.10.en: Who will rescue me from this famine but You, O satisfaction of my soul?!
